questions.question:
**Direction: Select the correct sentence in active voice from the following options.**

The police have been called by the neighbours.

options.text: The neighbours have called the police.
The police are being called by the neighbours.
The Police said to me, “I will call the neighbours.”
The police have been called by the neighbours.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The neighbours have called the police."**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The reason for selecting option 1, **"The neighbours have called the police,"** as the correct sentence in active voice is that it clearly presents the subject (the neighbours) performing the action (calling the police) directly.
 
• It follows the structure of the present perfect tense: **Subject + Has/have + V3 + Object**
 
• In active voice constructions, the subject takes the main position in the sentence and performs the action on the object.
 
• Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 1.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• In contrast, the other options either use passive voice (where the subject is receiving the action) or have a more convoluted structure:

 
 
• **Option 2 ("The police are being called by the neighbours")** is in passive voice, emphasizing the police as the receiver of the action.
 
• **Option 3 ("The Police said to me, 'I will call the neighbours.'")** introduces a reported speech structure and a future action, making it a different context.
 
• ​**Option 4 ("The police have been called by the neighbours")** is in passive voice, indicating that the police are the ones being acted upon rather than performing the action.

A. The other half had been sued at least twice, and Levinson found that just on the basis of those conversations, she could find clear differences between the two groups.

B. Recently the medical researcher Wendy Levinson recorded hundreds of conversations between a group of physicians and their patients.

C. The surgeons who had never been sued spent more than three minutes longer with each patient than those who had been sued did.

• **Sentence B** introduces the main activity – Wendy Levinson recording conversations between physicians and patients.
 
• **Sentence D** provides additional information about the doctors, stating that roughly half of them had never been sued.
 
• **Sentence A **builds on the information from sentence D, explaining that Levinson found clear differences between the two groups of doctors based on their conversations.
 
• **Sentence C** adds more specific details about the differences by stating that surgeons who had never been sued spent more time with each patient compared to those who had been sued.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 1.
 
• Correct sequence:​

B. Recently the medical researcher Wendy Levinson recorded hundreds of conversations between a group of physicians and their patients.

D. Roughly half of the doctors had never been sued.

A. The other half had been sued at least twice, and Levinson found that just on the basis of those conversations, she could find clear differences between the two groups.

C. The surgeons who had never been sued spent more than three minutes longer with each patient than those who had been sued did.

• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:

• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'We.'​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'teacher'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• 'Compelled' will be changed into 'was compelled'. 
 
• "Teacher" is a singular subject and we must use "was" with it.
 
• The preposition "by" is used to indicate the doer of the action in the passive voice.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.

 ​

Correct sentence: *The teacher was compelled to finish the class sooner.*
